newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Money injection news sends Seoul shrs to close up.
newsitem.headline: Money injection news sends Seoul shrs to close up.

text.p: Seoul shares ended higher on Monday on news the central bank would supply additional liquidity into the money market, brokers said.
The composite stock index provisionally closed at 687.25, 4.12 points higher. Decliners edged ahead of advancers by 393 to 368, while 141 went unchanged.
Brokers said the market was boosted by speculative buying by individual investors who felt the negative impact of the Hanbo Group's financial trouble had already been reflected.

"But institutional investors and fundamentalists want to see some improvement in economic numbers, which are still quite bad," said a Dongsuh Securities broker. This tug of war would cause the bourse to be volatile for the time being, he said.
On Saturday, the nation posted its largest ever monthly trade deficit of $3.48 billion for January.

The Bank of Korea said it would supply 1.2 trillion won this week through redemption of Monetary Stabilisation Bonds and 800 billion won through repurchase agreements with banks. It has already released a total of 3.6 trillion since late January when Hanbo Steel was declared insolvent.
"Individual shares led the buying earlier in the day, but then profit-taking emerged, eating away some of the gains," said analyst Lee Sang-koo of Hyundai Securities.
The most actively traded stock was SEOULBANK, which lost 90 won to 4,040. Korea First Bank also fell 90 won to 3,800.

Hanbo Steel, which is currently trading on the stock exchange's watch list, ended the day at its upper limit of 3,270 won, 1,800 higher. Hanbo, the flagship of the Hanbo Group, is seeking court receivership after piling up about five trillion won in loans.
